newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia tries Yugoslav army general in absentia.
newsitem.headline: Croatia tries Yugoslav army general in absentia.

text.p: The chief of staff of the Yugoslav army, General Momcilo Perisic, and 18 former fellow officers went on trial in Croatia in their absence on Thursday for alleged war crimes, state media reported.
A 20th defendant, a Bosnian Moslem, was taken into Croatian custody in August and was present for the start of the trial.

The state prosecutor's office in the Adriatic port of Zadar linked the 20 officers to a 1991 bombardment of the town by Yugoslav army (JNA) troops backing a minority Serb revolt against Croatia's secession from federal Yugoslavia.
Perisic was then a colonel commanding a JNA artillery training centre from which Zadar was shelled, the Croatian press agency HINA said earlier.
It said that 30 civilians were killed and more than 120 buildings suffered considerable damage in attacks ordered by Perisic and his aides.
Serb forces seized almost a third of Croatia by January 1992, when a ceasefire was signed. Croatian troops recaptured two of the three Serb-held enclaves in 1995 offensives.

HINA said the only defendant present at the trial was Mirsad Catic, who later became a Bosnian embassy official in Bonn. He was arrested in August at a border crossing with Italy and transferred to a Zadar prison.

"...In September and October 1991 Catic participated in artillery attacks on Zadar, issued orders to his subordinates to open artillery fire at parts of Zadar and he opened fire himself," HINA quoted the indictment as saying.
Prosecution witness Elvis Maras, a JNA soldier at the time, said he heard from another soldier that Catic personally ordered attacks on Zadar and had been more cruel than other JNA officers.
Catic denied the charges, claiming he had no commanding authority. He said he fired from the army barracks only at random with an automatic rifle.
HINA said the verdict would be delivered on Friday.
